constraints: Offline developer check of the currently tested Python installation against two static pyproject identity strings; Python 3.9/3.13 CI profile, Linux/macOS/Windows, no real-time or throughput requirement.
Reject duplicate identity headers without implementing an email parser or changing passport runtime, package metadata, wire contracts, normalization semantics or output shape.
alternatives: Python importlib.metadata with standard get_all header enumeration and existing TOML parser.
Python packaging.metadata parse_email/from_email for broader core-metadata validation.
Rust uv package/environment inspection with an interpreter probe for imported-module identity.
Java TomlJ plus Python metadata/import inspection for the actual installation under test.
rationale: KEEP direct interpreter inspection. The required observable is all identity headers in the selected distribution, not a package-list summary. The standard metadata object preserves duplicates and offers case-insensitive get_all; comparing its full list with one expected value supplies cardinality and equality together.

packaging.metadata is credible for complete metadata validation but would add a separate raw-metadata parsing/validation policy beyond this exact two-field check. Broader package metadata compliance should use an explicit separate requirement.

uv documents environment and package inspection; TomlJ provides Java TOML parsing. Neither cited interface establishes this same-interpreter imported-module and duplicate-header check. They remain credible for other packaging boundaries but provide no evidenced correctness or deployment advantage for this correction.

Two new real-file test methods cover single mixed-case headers and six duplicate combinations across Name/Version. Before correction, four duplicate cases were silently accepted; after correction, all six reject. Existing missing and mismatched field checks remain passing.

Selection is based on the observable and deployment boundaries, not installed tooling, rewrite cost or language familiarity. No alternate-runtime benchmark or universal performance ranking was performed.
limits: Trusted local metadata; not publisher authentication, a whole-metadata validator, loaded-bytecode attestation or atomic source/installation snapshot.
Exact project-profile strings remain required. Does not implement general equivalent-name/version normalization.
Local execution uses Linux Python 3.13 only. The Python 3.9 API documentation supports the chosen primitive but is not executed 3.9/Tomli or hosted matrix evidence.
No new build or install, physical qualification, MLS/CNSA, availability or complete-phase claim.
